items.title: Percy Heath — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: This old German prince told his sister… and after the performance, I have a tie pin with the family crest of Fürstenberg... He went to all of us and handed us this family crest, on a tie pin, of Fürstenberg.

ctx.x: Well, that scene was accompanied by a piece [by] John Lewis that the bass started, a real cortege it was to accompany that scene of this black, ebony gondola going down the Grand Canal in Venice. The scenes are fantastic in the movie, and it was filmed in Venice. This old German prince told his sister… and after the performance, I have a tie pin with the family crest of Fürstenberg. Of course, after the war, they were just name beer distributors, Fürstenberg beer. But to have this old German prince to come up…

Quartet. I don’t know nobody in jazz, that things like that never happened before. So we were not only pioneers with the music, but with (the) attire and never being late. We were ahead of time every gig we ever played. I think once something happened, transportation broke down, planes couldn’t leave on account of the weather and we were a little later getting to a job, but maybe twice in forty-something years.
